title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript leaf. It is a typed page (page 49 of Exposé IX, with the running page number 367) of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', §4.7. It belongs to the proof of the Galois criterion for semistable reduction.

Setting: A is an abelian variety over K, the fraction field of a henselian discrete valuation ring with residue field k.
- Claim: if Galois acts trivially on the n-torsion nA(K̄) for some n ≥ 3 prime to the residue characteristic, then A has semistable reduction over K, so K(nA) is a field of semistable reduction.
- Setup: reduce to S strictly local. Let K' be a finite Galois extension over which A acquires semistable reduction, with Γ = Gal(K'/K). Choose K' minimal, so that Γ acts faithfully on the connected Néron special fibre A_0^{*o}, which is an extension of an abelian variety by a torus.
- Γ acts trivially on nA(K̄), hence on its finite étale part nA(K̄)^{ef} ≅ nA_0^*(k), and so on nA_0^{*o}(k).

Lemma 4.7.1 (Serre): let G be an extension of an abelian scheme by a torus over a field and n ≥ 2. A finite-order automorphism acting trivially on nG is the identity if n ≠ 2, and has order at most 2 if n = 2.
Lemma 4.7.2: a finite group of exponent 2 is (Z/2)^r.
Together these force Γ = 1 when n ≥ 3.

Proof sketch begun in 4.7.3:
- Since n·id_G is an epimorphism, u|nG = id is equivalent to 1 − u = nv in End(G).
- Reduce to u of prime-power order p^N.
- Take a subring E of End(G). It is finite type and torsion-free because G is divisible, so it embeds in E⊗Q, a product of cyclotomic fields.
- The proof then continues with the standard argument (ζ − 1 divisible by n forces ζ = 1, or ζ = −1 when n = 2).
errors: The text says 'E le sous-anneau de End(G) engendré par v, qui est un quotient de Z[T]/(T^{p^N}−1)'. It is the subring generated by u that is a quotient of Z[T]/(T^{p^N}−1). The ring generated by v is a quotient of Z[T]/((1−nT)^{p^N}−1). Its finiteness over Z follows instead from End(G) being a finitely generated Z-module. This is a minor slip, possibly present in the printed SGA 7 text as well.

ideas.what: Galois action trivial on n-torsion (n≥3) implies semistable reduction; minimal K' acts faithfully on the special fibre
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Raynaud criterion for semistable reduction (SGA 7 IX 4.7)

ideas.what: Finite-order automorphism trivial on n-torsion is trivial for n≥3, of order ≤2 for n=2
ideas.modern_name: Serre's lemma (rigidity of level-n structures, Minkowski-type)

ideas.what: Exponent-2 finite group is elementary abelian

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript page of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX §4.7, published in 1972 and well known. It has apparently been misfiled in this folder of 1976 manuscript notes on the divided-power de Rham complex.
transcription_corrections: The page is typed, not handwritten. It is SGA 7 Exposé IX, page 49, numbered 367 at the foot. The pencilled '212' is the archive folio number.
The transcription is essentially accurate. 'A_o^{*o}' denotes the identity component of the Néron special fibre A_0^*.
